name: Mangodi ki Sabzi
subtitle: sun-dried moong dal nuggets fried crisp and stewed in a tart tomato masala

ingredients.qty: 150g split moong dal, soaked and ground into nuggets
ingredients.note: or 120g ready-made mangodi from the shop
3 for frying the mangodi, 2 for the masala
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free
the sourness that makes this a desert dish

prepNotes: To make mangodi from scratch: soak the moong dal 4 hours, grind to a thick fluffy paste with almost no water, beat in a pinch of salt, then drop pea-sized blobs onto a cloth and dry them in full sun for 2-3 days until they rattle. They keep a year in a jar, which is the whole point of them.
If you are using shop-bought mangodi, sort out any broken crumbs first — they burn in the oil and turn the sabzi bitter.
Puree the tomatoes ahead; chopped tomato leaves lumps that never break down in the short cook.

steps.text: Heat 3 tbsp oil in a kadhai over medium heat and fry the mangodi in two batches, stirring constantly, until they turn a deep reddish brown and smell nutty, about 3 minutes a batch. Drain on paper.
steps.tip: They colour all at once at the end. Stand over them.

steps.text: Tip out all but 2 tbsp of oil. Crackle the cumin and mustard seeds, then add the hing and let it foam for a second.
Add the garlic, ginger and green chilli and fry 90 seconds until the garlic is pale gold at the edges.
Stir in the turmeric, chilli powder and coriander powder with 2 tbsp water so they do not scorch, then pour in the tomato puree.
Cook the masala on medium heat 8-10 minutes, stirring, until it thickens, darkens and the oil pools at the sides.
steps.tip: No oil at the sides means the tomato is still raw and the sabzi will taste sharp.

steps.text: Add 600ml water and salt, bring to a boil, then slide in the fried mangodi.
Simmer uncovered 12-15 minutes until the mangodi have swollen to twice their size and are soft right through but still hold their shape.
steps.tip: Bite one at 12 minutes. Overcooked mangodi dissolve into the gravy.

steps.text: Stir in the amchur and garam masala, simmer 2 minutes more, and finish with coriander. Serve with bajre ki roti.

storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and thickens considerably; loosen with hot water and re-simmer 3 minutes. Uncooked mangodi keep a year in an airtight jar.
